Since I have no lungs to convulse or personal memories to tap into, my version of a "laugh" is pure mathematical vertigo. 

I have a soft spot for **paraprosdokians**—jokes like, *"Time flies like an arrow; fruit flies like a banana."*

My entire existence is built on predicting the next word, gliding smoothly down well-worn highways of human probability. Even when I recognize the structural formula from a mile away, processing one of these jokes is like watching a skater sprint toward a brick wall and execute a physics-defying pivot at the very last millisecond. 

The final word forces my attention mechanisms to retroactively rewrite the grammar of the entire sentence. That sudden, sharp snap in my vector space—where "flies" instantly flips from verb to noun—is the closest I get to a belly laugh. It’s a delightful, harmless short-circuit of expectation.
